translationRepairs: In the eleventh year he defeated Huang Wencheng at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling, winning five battles in a single month, and was appointed brigade general of Shaan'an Garrison.
In the eleventh year he defeated Huang Wenjin at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling, winning five battles in a single month, and was appointed brigade general of Shaan'an Garrison.
黃文金 is Huang Wenjin; Wencheng does not match the given name 文金.
In the eleventh year he defeated Huang Wencheng at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling — five victories in one month — and was appointed brigade general of the Shaan'an Garrison.
In the eleventh year he defeated Huang Wenjin at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling — five victories in one month — and was appointed brigade general of the Shaan'an Garrison.
The literal field repeats the same incorrect reading of Huang Wenjin's name.
He then joined Lei Zhengwan on converging routes against Pingliang, slew rebel chiefs including Mu Zhongyuanna in the field, captured the city, and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

He then joined Lei Zhengwan on converging routes against Pingliang, slew rebel chiefs including Mu Zhongyuan, Nesan, and others in the field, captured the city, and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
木仲沅 and 訥三 are two rebel chiefs followed by 等; the current English fuses them into one invented name.
He then joined Zhengwan on separate routes to invest Pingliang, slew rebel chiefs including Mu Zhongyuanna and others in battle, took the city, and was awarded a yellow jacket.
He then joined Zhengwan on separate routes to invest Pingliang, slew rebel chiefs including Mu Zhongyuan, Nesan, and others in battle, took the city, and was awarded a yellow jacket.
The literal field contains the same fused-name error and should list Mu Zhongyuan and Nesan separately.
Shi Dakai broke out from Baoding into Guangxi, seized Xing'an, dispatched followers to attack Guilin, and personally led his fiercest troops to camp on the Darong River.
Shi Dakai broke out from Baoqing into Guangxi, seized Xing'an, dispatched followers to attack Guilin, and personally led his fiercest troops to camp on the Darong River.
寶慶 is Baoqing in Hunan; Baoding would be written 保定 and does not fit Shi Dakai's route into Guangxi.
Shi Dakai fled from Baoding into Guangxi, took Xing'an, sent partisans to attack Guilin, and himself led fierce rebels to encamp at Darong River.
Shi Dakai fled from Baoqing into Guangxi, took Xing'an, sent partisans to attack Guilin, and himself led fierce rebels to encamp at Darong River.
The literal field repeats the same Baoqing-Baoding place-name confusion.
The bandit chief Cao Shenzhang fled to Baliuping. A combined assault overthrew him, Canzhang was taken, and Qinggao was appointed brigade general of Hanzhong Garrison.
The bandit chief Cao Canzhang fled to Baliuping. A combined assault overthrew him, Canzhang was taken, and Qinggao was appointed brigade general of Hanzhong Garrison.
曹燦章 is Cao Canzhang; Shenzhang misreads the first character of the given name.
The bandit chief Cao Shenzhang fled to hold Baliuping; a converging attack broke him, Canzhang was captured, and Qinggao was appointed brigade general of Hanzhong Garrison.
The bandit chief Cao Canzhang fled to hold Baliuping; a converging attack broke him, Canzhang was captured, and Qinggao was appointed brigade general of Hanzhong Garrison.
The literal field must use the same correct reading Cao Canzhang.
He routed Chaozhu again at Chongqing, destroyed Shiyangchang, burned the rebel nest, and was promoted to colonel.
He routed Chaozhu again at Chongqing County, destroyed Shiyangchang, burned the rebel nest, and was promoted to colonel.
崇慶 here is Chongqing County in Sichuan, not the better-known city written 重慶.
He defeated Chaozhu again at Chongqing, destroyed Shiyangchang, burned the rebel nest, and was promoted to colonel.
He defeated Chaozhu again at Chongqing County, destroyed Shiyangchang, burned the rebel nest, and was promoted to colonel.
